A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MonteCLoRA research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and included appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated proofs. The separate supplementary derivations referenced by v3 are outside the supplied evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original RoBERTa and LLaMA experiments, hyperparameter sensitivity measurements, component ablations, convergence curves and computational benchmarks.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds larger NLU tasks, mathematical reasoning, code generation and computational measurements across additional models.

M1.justification: The core reparameterization, training losses and sampling-free inference remain. Section 7.2 introduces an optimized training procedure that pre-generates samples, caches them and replenishes the buffer when exhausted, replacing sampling within each forward pass for the computational study. The revised Gaussian description otherwise clarifies the existing weighted-sampling procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds SST2, QNLI, QQP and MNLI to the original five NLU tasks. It also introduces mathematical reasoning on GSM8k and functional code generation on HumanEval, with a Magicoder-OSS-Instruct training subset. The original six commonsense tasks remain.

E2.justification: LoRA+, IA3 and Prompt Tuning become evaluated comparators in v3 Tables 10–11, alongside LoRA and DoRA. Existing NLU, commonsense and Bayesian comparisons remain. The replacement computational comparison drops the full-fine-tuning comparator present in v1 Table 10.

E3.justification: The original hyperparameter grid in Table 3 is retained. New evaluations introduce LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct, strict-match and flexible-extract scoring for GSM8k, and HumanEval pass@2/pass@4. The computational study changes from RoBERTa on WiC to buffered sampling on CoLA and HumanEval across additional models, with new sequence lengths, module configurations and a 1,000-step LLaMA budget.

E4.justification: The original component, initialization, sparsity, module-placement, post-hoc and convergence analyses are retained despite renumbering. v3 extends hyperparameter-sensitivity analysis to larger NLU tasks and math/code generation, including Figure 6. It also replaces the computational analysis with model-scale and buffered-sampling comparisons, dropping the earlier four-versus-eight-sample cost comparison.

E5.justification: v1 Table 10 reports runtime and memory with ± uncertainty values; v3 Table 12 reports only relative point estimates. Section 6.1 retains Wilcoxon testing for extrinsic robustness but no longer reports the intrinsic-robustness test. Neither version specifies experimental seed or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: The original five-task NLU entries and six-task commonsense tables remain unchanged. Added NLU tasks change aggregate rankings: v1 Table 6 favors MonteCLoRA at 81.7 versus full fine-tuning at 80.1, whereas v3's expanded average favors full fine-tuning at 84.6 versus 84.4. These are different task aggregates, not performance changes under identical coverage. v3 also adds GSM8k/HumanEval results and replaces the computational measurements under different settings.

T1.justification: v3 Equation 6 replaces the Gaussian-mixture density expression with a weighted-sample expression and adds Lemma 4.6 linking cooperative loss to entropy minimization. It omits the explicit SGD assumptions/rate discussion and standalone introductory Monte Carlo proof. Detailed KL-divergence proofs in v1 Appendix A.3 become formulas and a reference to separate supplementary material. The principal unbiasedness and variance arguments remain; the Gaussian-noise lemma and two background proofs are relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the additional-parameter claim from O(1) to O(r), and replaces gains of up to 3.8% accuracy and 8.6% robustness with 0.5% and 1.6% over unregularized low-rank adaptation. It changes the generative claim from lower variance to lower spread and extends it to LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct. These revise the scope and substance of the efficiency and performance claims.

C2.justification: v3 expands the distinction between median robustness and outlier-sensitive spread, adds a Gaussian-sampling mechanism discussion and explains sampling-cost amortization. New Sections 7.3–7.4 explicitly discuss sampling overhead, hardware dependence, additional hyperparameter tuning, scaling limits and possible extensions. These materially expand qualifications and applicability discussion beyond v1's scattered caveats.

D1.justification: v3 documents buffered sampling with a buffer size of 15, its replenishment procedure and detailed computational-benchmark settings. It adds the LLaMA-3.2 sample scaler, LM-evaluation-harness usage and the Python/length filtering and 10,000-example sampling recipe for code training. It also explicitly identifies M=1 in Algorithm 1. The code-access link and original hardware disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: References and discussion expand to cover LoRA+, Prompt Tuning, newer models, GSM8k, HumanEval, Magicoder and the evaluation harness. Citations to Agarwal et al., Sengupta et al. and Garrigos and Gower disappear. The central positioning against conventional PEFT and post-hoc Laplace-LoRA remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the theoretical exposition: it moves the Gaussian-noise lemma into Background, relocates background proofs to Appendix A, condenses distribution descriptions and KL derivations, and restructures the appendices into A–E. It also rewrites the abstract and substantial results/efficiency passages, and adds dedicated rationale, limitations and future-work sections.

P2.justification: The document adopts a wider layout and different typography and headers. Figure 1 becomes a two-panel comparison including MonteCLoRA; Figure 4 and Tables 5–6 expand to nine tasks. New Figure 6 and Tables 10–11 display math/code evaluations, while Table 12 replaces the absolute-cost table with model-wise overhead ratios. Several retained plots are restyled or relocated.

improvement.justification: Broader evaluations, narrower headline claims and explicit limitations improve the paper's empirical scope and candor. However, the new Lemma 4.6 incorrectly decomposes the entropy of a weighted sum into component entropies, and the runtime prose conflicts with Table 12: its 8B All setting reports 1.53× runtime and 1.23× memory, exceeding the stated bounds. Computational uncertainty reporting also disappears. These substantive gains and new reliability problems prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
